summary: One POST form at /login/ on the connection's own origin. The template writes the form, the two labels and the button; the two inputs are rendered from Django's standard authentication form.

sources.title: NetBox 4.7.2 login view: the form is Django's AuthenticationForm; the route is login/ (netbox/netbox/urls.py line 21)
Django 6.1.1, the version NetBox pins: AuthenticationForm has a text field username and a password field password
Django 6.1.1 input template: type, name and the widget attributes are written on an input element
NetBox 4.7.2 authentication tests: post the fields username and password to the login view

Django 6.1.1 bound field: the input's name is the field name (line 20) and its id comes from the form's auto_id pattern (lines 96-98, 244-254), which django/forms/forms.py line 77 sets to id_ followed by the name
Django 6.1.1 widgets: TextInput has the type text (line 434), PasswordInput the type password (line 469)
NetBox 4.7.2 requirements: Django is pinned to exactly 6.1.1

selectors.note: Each single sign-on backend is its own form with its own submit button (lines 94-104), so the button is tied to the form that holds the password field.

staysInteractive.note: Configured backends are extra forms under the login form. With the login form hidden by configuration only those remain, and the login stops as a layout mismatch.

schemaGaps: An installation with a base path serves the page at that prefix followed by login/. The format has no path-suffix or installation-relative gate, and these are Django's generic field ids, so the gate stays: only an installation at the host root is covered. Under a base path nothing is filled.
notes: The template has the same form, labels and button, and the view the same Django form, at 4.0.11, 4.2.9 and 4.4.10 (read at those tags on 2026-10-12). Release 3.7.8 uses its own form class and a template without the labels; it was not reviewed further and may not match. No second factor is part of this login in the source read.
